Codex all-provider replay still needs schema alignment with latest app-server behavior before it can be treated as a full-suite signal. ## Closes Verified against the branch with code/commit evidence. ### High confidence Closes #4952 Closes #4873 Closes #4775 Closes #4795 Closes #4710 Closes #4668 Closes #4619 Closes #4584 Closes #4561 Closes #4713 Closes #4198 Closes #4452 Closes #3797 Closes #4232 Closes #3666 Closes #3580 Closes #2785 Closes #2789 Closes #3138 Closes #1404 Closes #231 Closes #216 ### Medium confidence (under review) Closes #4568 Closes #4766 Closes #4495 Closes #4456 Closes #4399 Closes #3744 Closes #2921 Closes #3624 Closes #3149 Closes #2336 Closes #538 Closes #2173 Closes #2065 > [!NOTE] > ### Introduce orchestration V2 runtime, services, provider adapters, and MCP toolkits > - Adds a complete orchestration V2 server runtime: projection store, event store, effect outbox, command receipts, checkpoint capture/rollback, thread management, run execution, provider session management, context handoff, runtime policy, and legacy V1 thread importer, composed through [runtimeLayer.ts](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/pull/2829/files#diff-30c4fe2818a050e1c3b89d70f25bba98ae53c42a26c7ab2fe70598ea812dd052) > - Adds V2 provider adapters for Codex, Claude, Cursor, Grok, OpenCode, and ACP Registry with a shared adapter contract, driver registry, and selection-transition policy > - Adds MCP toolkit services and HTTP registration for orchestrator delegation, thread operations, worktree handoff, project lifecycle, attachments, environment preferences, and preview controls > - Adds scheduled-task persistence, scheduling logic, server service, client runtime atoms, and a settings UI surface > - Migrates client-runtime and web/mobile UI from legacy session/turn fields to V2 projection-based runtime/run state, including thread details panel, queue controls, relationship graph, history loading, and item inspector > - Registers database migrations 050–061 for V2 foundation tables, subagents, provider-session bindings, launch workflows, application event sourcing, effect cancellation, scheduled tasks, legacy import state, and recovery/shell indexes > - Risk: replaces the legacy `EnvironmentApi` orchestration interface with `orchestrationV2`; removes `serverUpdateThreadContinuation` capability; `CursorSettings` no longer exposes `binaryPath` or `apiEndpoint`; `ProviderUsageLimitsIngestionLive` no longer subscribes to runtime events; thread routing resolves existing non-deleted threads directly to ready instead of loading > > > > Macroscope summarized 6102d00. > > --- > [!NOTE] > **Medium Risk** > Mobile thread persistence and list/archive/stop behavior change with V2 runtime semantics; removing the thread-transfer report workflow reduces PR visibility into transfer budget regressions. > > **Overview** > This slice of the orchestration V2 rollout **retires the thread-transfer PR comment pipeline** (trusted publisher script, tests, and `workflow_run` workflow) while CI can still emit transfer artifacts; it also **installs `build-essential` in CI** so ACP process-tree fixtures compile instead of soft-skipping. > > **Mobile** moves onto shared V2 client-runtime pieces: SQLite cache uses `ORCHESTRATION_CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION` and stored V2 shell/thread snapshots, runtime wiring swaps in bounded thread snapshot loading and history control, and thread detail/review/archive flows read **projections** (`runtime`, `RuntimeRequestId`, checkpoint summaries from `runId`) instead of V1 session/turn shapes. UX additions include **activity inspector**, **queue control**, **relationships banner**, progressive **history controls**, server **visit** watermarking, stricter **archive** rules via `threadCanArchive`, and approval/user-input cards that honor **live vs dead** provider `responseCapability`. > > Smaller touches: shared **brand mark** module, new **uniwind adaptive color** tokens, desktop env test for user-data dir names, README link to appearance docs, and marketing copy for Cursor harness. > > Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 9eeed8c17109be3752d2f8e1643583d1f579ea2d. ## Provider-initiated turns are invisible: post-turn SDK activity is dropped entirely

Two reproductions today (threads `47763f5e`, `71e29ba5`), one root cause. Filing here since the fix is squarely in turn-mapping territory; relates to the `t3code/scheduled-tasks` follow-up "thread-bound fires steer active turns".

### Symptom

A thread shows **finished** in the UI while the Claude SDK session is actively running a turn — making tool calls, pushing to PRs. The work is invisible: no run, no turn items, no activity log entries, nothing in `orchestration_events` after the last user-requested turn completed.

### Repro timelines

**Thread `47763f5e`** (background-task wakeup):
- `22:10:01` — turn completes (`result`, end_turn: "…polling every minute, up to 25 min"). Run ordinal 9 → `completed`, session → `ready`. Last orchestration event for the thread.
- `22:12:56` — SDK wakes the session: `system/task_updated` + `system/task_notification` (watcher task `bdknlk0tp` completed) → `system/init` → full new streaming turn with tool calls (visible in the provider protocol log only).
- Several minutes of real work (incl. `git push`) with **zero** orchestration events.

**Thread `71e29ba5`** (ScheduleWakeup self-pacing loop):
- `22:36:13` — run 58 completes with `stop_reason: "tool_use"` (agent called `ScheduleWakeup` and went to sleep). Last orchestration event.
- `22:36:49` — `task_updated` (status `failed`!) + `task_notification` for `blrc0l01r` → `system/init` → new turn.
- `22:37:55` — invisible turn completes (~66s, 8 SDK turns), calls `ScheduleWakeup` again. Loop repeats: one invisible turn per wakeup. No run 59 exists.

### Root cause chain

1. **Adapter** (`ClaudeAdapter.ts`): `context.turnState` is created only by `sendTurn` (orchestrator-requested prompt) and cleared in `handleResultMessage`. When the SDK starts a turn on its own (task-notification wakeup), there is no `turnState`, so `handleStreamEvent` early-returns and drops everything streamed. The synthetic-turn fallback in `handleAssistantMessage` (~L2468) triggers too late (first complete assistant message) and demonstrably did not rescue either repro.
2. **Ingestion** (`ProviderRuntimeIngestion.ts`): a `turn.started` with no active turn would be *accepted* (session → `running`), but no run exists — ordinals/`userMessageId`/provider-turn binding all come from `thread.turn-start-requested`, so turn-scoped events have nowhere to project.
3. **Bonus bug**: the adapter has no `system/task_updated` case — it falls through to the unknown-message default. 7 occurrences in one thread, including `failed` and `killed` status patches, all dropped as "unknown SDK message" warnings.

### Proposed fix

1. **Orchestrator: mint runs for turns nobody requested.** In `processRuntimeEvent`, when an accepted `turn.started` has no pending turn-start (`getPendingTurnStartByThreadId` → `None`), dispatch a `run.provider-initiated` command: next ordinal from the same counter, no `userMessageId`, `trigger` payload from the event, provider-turn→run binding as if a pending turn-start had been claimed. Key on `turnId` for replay idempotency. Everything downstream (turn items, messages, checkpoints, `turn.completed` → run completed) reuses existing projection code.
2. **Adapter: open the turn at the wakeup signal, not the first assistant message.** On `stream_event/message_start` (or `system/status: requesting`) with `turnState === undefined`, create a synthetic `turnState` and emit `turn.started` with trigger metadata. Keep the assistant-message fallback as a safety net.
3. **Schedule fires (t3code/scheduled-tasks): front door when idle.** A thread-bound fire hitting a thread with no active turn should go through the normal turn-start pipeline (synthetic user message), not silently steer the idle session. Keep steer for genuinely-active turns. (Doesn't cover SDK-internal wakeups — hence 1+2.)
4. **Adapter: handle `system/task_updated`** — apply the patch to `claudeTasks` state / emit a task-updated runtime event instead of dropping failed/killed statuses.
5. **Observability:** loud warning when a decoded SDK message arrives while session status is `ready` with no `turnState`. This was only diagnosable by diffing the provider protocol log against the event store.

### Gift from the SDK

The post-wakeup `result` already carries `"origin": {"kind": "task-notification"}` — the SDK explicitly labels provider-initiated turns. The adapter can carry `origin` straight into the synthetic `turn.started` payload and the run record; no correlation heuristics needed.

UI implication: a run with `trigger: "provider"` renders with a trigger header ("resumed: background task completed / schedule fired") instead of a user bubble, and the thread correctly shows running during autonomous work.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Follow-up: post-turn wakeup handling implemented (design revised)

Implemented on this branch (`t3code/codex-turn-mapping`), with one significant revision to the plan in my earlier comment after re-reading the raw provider chunks: **not every wakeup should become a new run.** The SDK distinguishes two cases, and they now get different treatment:

### 1. ScheduleWakeup sleep loops — adapter-only, no orchestrator involvement
The recorded chunks are explicit: the yield result carries `stop_reason: "tool_use"` (not `end_turn`), and the ScheduleWakeup tool result carries structured `{scheduledFor, clampedDelaySeconds}` plus prose ("Nothing more to do this turn — the harness re-invokes you…"). `ClaudeAdapterV2` now tracks the observed ScheduleWakeup result on the turn context and **does not finalize** such turns: the run stays active, run-scoped ingestion stays subscribed, and the wakeup continuation streams into the same run. A 25-minute poll loop is one run, not a run per wakeup.

### 2. True `end_turn` re-invocations — provider-initiated runs
When Claude genuinely ends the turn and the SDK later re-invokes it (background task notification), holding the run open is wrong (dev servers run forever), so:
- `ClaudeAdapterV2` buffers the post-turn activity (skipping stream-event noise) and emits a new `turn.wakeup` adapter event once real activity starts, with `origin` extracted from the `task_notification`.
- `ProviderWakeupService` (new): relay queue + daemon (breaks the session-manager ↔ orchestrator layer cycle). The daemon **waits for thread quiescence** (the wakeup announce races the previous run's terminal commit by milliseconds), then dispatches `message.dispatch` with new mode **`attach_wakeup`**.
- The orchestrator mints a run through the existing dispatch machinery — synthetic message (`createdBy: "system"`, `creationSource: "provider"`, turn item `inputIntent: "provider_wakeup"`) — and `RunExecutionService` delivers via the new optional adapter method **`attachTurn`** (adopt in-flight turn + replay buffer; nothing sent to the provider).
- Guards: superseded by any blocking run; no provider switch; no pending context transfers. A user turn that races the wakeup wins; the adapter drops its buffer (task bookkeeping is still applied).

### 3. Backgrounded commands (`Bash` + `run_in_background`)
Previously these projected as *completed* `command_execution` items the instant the tool returned, while the command kept running. Now: a tool result carrying `tool_use_result.backgroundTaskId` keeps the item **`running`**, registered session-level; the matching `task_updated` flips it terminal (killed/failed no longer dropped — there was no `task_updated` handling at all), and `task_notification` enriches the output with the summary. This works cross-run: `routeProviderEvent` accepts item/node updates for owned provider threads, so a wakeup run can complete an earlier run's item.

### Tests
New replay fixture **`claude_provider_wakeup`** built frame-by-frame from the recorded thread `47763f5e` chunks (watcher task, second `init`, `message_start` announce, `origin: task-notification` result). It drives the full loop end-to-end: replay stream → adapter buffer/announce → session-manager pump → wakeup relay → `attach_wakeup` dispatch → run minting → `attachTurn` replay → cross-run background-command completion → follow-up user turn. New fixture step `await_provider_wakeup_run` awaits daemon-minted runs. Full orchestration-v2 suite green (273 tests; all 69 pre-existing replay fixtures unchanged).

### Known follow-ups
- Session idle reaper (30 min) vs long scheduled sleeps (ScheduleWakeup clamps to 60 min) — a session could be reaped mid-sleep.
- Superseded wakeup buffers replay only task bookkeeping; the dropped wakeup turn's content is lost for that round (logged).
- `OrchestrationV2ProviderTurn` has no `waiting` status literal — held-open turns read as `running`; consider adding `waiting` for honest UI during sleeps.
- UI: render `inputIntent: "provider_wakeup"` turn items as a resume marker instead of a user bubble.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

I really want this feature, so I thought I’d help out by testing it. So far in testing it for an hour I haven’t had any major issues. I found several small things that I noticed. Feel free to use/ignore at your own discretion: **What I noticed** A queued message is both shown above the input box but also in the chat history. This confused me briefly at first. Because I thought the message was already sent directly. Really like the interrupt UI. Maybe a bit harsh of a harsh red color. Feels like “Interrupt requested -> Run interrupted” is doubled up. “Running” is not distinct and different copy than the sidebar “Working”. Would it make sense to harmonize those UIs? Currently it is hard to see at a glance which ones are running. Also it kept in "Running" even though the agents were done. ￼ I didn’t see a way to see which model is being used for the subagents. This is also annoying in Cursor, so would be nice plus if you get it right. This is relevant because Fable is expensive and I don’t really want the subagents to be Fable either. It is nice to easily see if my CLAUDE.md is working correctly. The lineage UI is confusing to me. When going back the ‘action’ icon is on the left. But when going into a child it is on the right. Also took me a while to notice the muted ‘this is a fork’ icon: ￼
Had a bug where the tool calls were not in the correct location: Default view After opening "Worked for 2m 7s"

I've also been doing work on this, especially with Claude 5 and GPT 5.6 models heavily using sub-agents

I'm thinking about adding a toggle to the sidebar to enable or disable viewing sub-agents from the sidebar.

The work here on delegate_task and create_thread are *huge* wins for my workflow as well. I've got some in-flight work integrating Orchestrator V2 into the mobile app and it's honestly incredible.

Thanks @juliusmarminge. I'll get a few smaller PRs opened against this PR. I'll put up my work on the mobile app but it's probably going to need rebasing once everything lands.

## Scheduled task reports success while its new-thread launch fails in background

Tested on `aec85c546e597dbcf78db81b134e7438d9a5ada3` with a scheduled task configured to create a new worktree. Reproduced twice with fresh threads.

### Observed

The scheduled-task record ends with `lastRunStatus: succeeded`, but the generated thread has ordinal 1 failed before provider start:

```text
Workspace preparation failed during generate metadata:
Text generation failed in generateBranchName: Failed to write temp file

ENOENT: no such file or directory, open
/tmp/t3code-codex-schema-208069-6MZJpS/919af017300b
```

The first reproduction used a custom `TMPDIR`; I restarted the desktop/server with `TMPDIR=/tmp` and confirmed the active server process inherited it. The second reproduction failed identically, so this is not caused by that local temp configuration, permissions, or available space.

### Status propagation

`ScheduledTaskService.runTask` treats `threadLaunch.launch(...)` returning as completion and immediately derives `lastRunStatus` from that `Exit`. `ThreadLaunchService.launch` returns successfully after `schedulePreparation(...)` forks `prepareInBackground` into `preparationScope`. When `generateBranchName` later fails, the prepared run/thread is marked failed, but that failure cannot update the already-completed scheduled-task run.

This creates two user-visible problems:

1. A recoverable branch-name metadata failure prevents the scheduled task from starting at all.
2. The scheduled task still reports success because it tracks dispatch rather than background preparation outcome.

Local workaround confirmed from the launch conditions: choose `Use the project checkout` or `Use a specific checkout`; both bypass the implicit worktree branch-name generation path. New-worktree scheduled tasks remain broken in this environment.

Suggested direction: await a preparation receipt/outcome before completing the scheduled-task run, and either fall back to `fallbackBranchName(threadId)` when branch-name generation fails or otherwise make metadata failure non-fatal.

[claude]

## Independent verification: this branch fixes #4198 (idle reaper vs. background work)

Adding a tested-on-sha data point since #4198 is in the high-confidence closes list.

### Real-world impact of the bug (0.0.31, macOS)

Forensics on one long-lived thread in my production `state.sqlite`: over ~18 h, the provider session was stopped and resumed **5 times** (`orchestration_events`: `thread.session-set status=stopped` → later `provider.operation:start-session` with `resume_cursor.source: "persisted"`). Each time, every process-local watcher/poller died with the session while the detached work it was watching (Codex CLI jobs, k8s jobs) kept running and completed fine — the next turn just showed *"No completion record was found for background agent…"* and the agent had to manually rediscover results by job id. Sessions that never crossed a stop/resume boundary completed background work cleanly, which matches the reaper being the trigger.

### Code-level verification at `f0e1196`

- `ProviderSessionReaper` (all three files) is removed.
- `orchestration-v2/ProviderSessionManager.ts` keeps the 30-min idle release (`DEFAULT_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS`) but `releaseIfStillIdle` now probes the adapter's `hasPendingBackgroundWork` first; pending work defers release (`idle-release-deferred`), re-checked each idle window, bounded by `DEFAULT_MAX_IDLE_PIN_MS` (4 h → `idle-release-pin-expired`).
- `ClaudeAdapterV2` pins on exactly the states that were lost before: pending background tasks per native thread, `running` subagents, and undrained wake buffers; `hasPendingBackgroundWorkForThread` gates the root-run stop path in `RunExecutionService`.

### Test run (macOS arm64, node 26, pnpm 11.10.0, sha `f0e1196`)

```
vp test run src/orchestration-v2/ProviderSessionManager.test.ts            → 25/25 passed
vp test run src/orchestration-v2/ProviderRuntimeRecoveryService*.test.ts   → 10/10 passed
```

incl. the pin-specific cases: *defers idle release while background work is pending*, *releases pinned idle sessions once the pin cap expires*, *does not apply a stale idle pin to a replacement session*.

### One note

The 4 h `maxIdlePinMs` cap means a background job longer than 4 h with zero foreground activity still gets released mid-run. That's a sane bound, but worth a line in the docs (and the `idle-release-pin-expired` warning is the right breadcrumb). From my side, this branch resolves the failure mode in #4198. 🚀

@juliusmarminge Based on communications I've seen on twitter and elsewhere, it seems that this branch is, in some sense "the future" of t3code. I'm wondering why, then, it is kept in a constant state of conflict with main. Presumably, the two will have to be reconciled, at some point, right?

As someone who maintains a somewhat substantial set of patches on top of upstream t3code, its a bit difficult to know how to proceed with maintaining these. I don't mind not getting any of my stuff merged ever, but it would be nice to understand roughly where things are headed with this branch, because a lot of the patches that I have touch the surface of what is going on here, and its difficult to know what exactly I should be tracking...

Hey, just came across an issue with scheduled tasks for remote projects. The UI lets me select a project from another environment, but the task is created and executed in the local environment. Since it only stores the `projectId`, the local server tries to find the remote project in its own database, and the run fails with `Project not found`. I think the task should be routed to the selected project’s environment, or the project picker should only show projects from the environment where the task will run.

A key use case for provider switching is quota exhaustion. When a user reaches the usage limit of the active model or provider during a long-running session, T3 Code should allow switching to another authenticated provider without losing the thread context, current worktree, pending plan, or file-change state.

Ideally, the limit error should offer a direct **Continue with another provider** action. If full context replay is unavailable, T3 Code could generate and transfer a structured handoff automatically.

### Bug: delegated-task completion wakes are silently starved after two deliveries per cohort — parent waits forever on the third wave

**TL;DR.** `delegate_task` (async) promises the parent a wake on every child terminal, and its tool description tells the agent to *"end the turn instead of polling."* But `finalizeDelegatedCompletionDelivery` refuses to reserve a follow-up delivery once a cohort has settled **two** deliveries (`settledDeliveryCount < 2`). Any child whose completion lands in a third wave stays `completionDelivery: "pending"` forever: no wake, no queued message, nothing on restart. The orchestrating agent — following the tool contract — sits idle waiting for a completion that already happened. With 4–5+ parallel children whose completions straddle wake turns, this is close to guaranteed.

Observed on the #7211 stack (V2 snapshot of 2026-08-28); everything cited below is `apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/` code from this PR's branch (none of it exists on `main`), and none of it is provider-specific.

### The two contracts that collide

`OrchestratorMcpService.ts`, delegate-task creation:

```ts
// Async delegations wake the parent on every child terminal; wait
// delegations deliver through the blocking tool call, so a wake is
// only needed if the parent settled first (timeout, disconnect).
completionWake: input.mode === "wait" ? "settled_only" : "always",
```

`Orchestrator.ts`, `planDelegatedCompletionDelivery`:

```ts
const settledDeliveryCount = cohort?.settledDeliveryCount ?? 0;
if (settledDeliveryCount >= 2) {
  // A cohort permits one initial delivery and one successor. Keep the
  // result pending and inspectable instead of recursively re-arming the
  // parent for every child that finishes after that bounded handoff.
  ...state: "pending"..., offer: false
```

…and the same `settledDeliveryCount < 2` guard in `finalizeDelegatedCompletionDelivery`'s `canReserveFollowUp`, which is the sweep that runs when a wake turn settles. `settledDeliveryCount` never resets, so this isn't a throttle — it's lifetime starvation per cohort. Nothing ever revisits a `"pending"` task after the cap engages: `handleTerminalRun` only sweeps delivery runs, the startup recovery path re-runs the same capped sweep, and `finalizeAppOwnedSubagent` early-returns on `existingResultTransfer`. The tool description ("An async child's completion wakes this thread… end the turn instead of polling") makes the failure mode maximally quiet: the agent does exactly what it was told and hangs.

### Forensic timeline (real thread, from `orchestration_v2_projection_*`)

Parent thread delegated 5 async children in one turn (run 7), so all 5 share run 7's cohort. Timestamps from the projections DB:

| time (UTC) | event | cohort state |
|---|---|---|
| 01:01:52 | run 7 delegates t10, t11, t13, t15, t17 | — |
| 01:05:49 | t10 completes → delivery 1, wake run 8 starts | `settled=0`, delivery gen 1 |
| 01:05:56–01:07:01 | t17, t13, t15 complete during run 8 → `"pending"` | |
| 01:07:11 | run 8 settles → sweep reserves delivery 2 = {t15, t17, t13} → wake run 9 starts 01:07:12 | `settled=1`, delivery gen 2 |
| **01:07:20** | **t11 completes, 8s into run 9 → `"pending"`** | |
| 01:09:12 | run 9 settles → sweep: `settledDeliveryCount` → 2, `pendingTaskIds = [t11]`, but `canReserveFollowUp` requires `< 2` → **refused** | `settled=2`, delivery `null`, t11 pending |
| 01:09–01:29 | parent idle; t11's result queryable but no wake exists or ever will | |
| 01:29:48 | human notices the stall and nudges; that run reads `task_status` → t11 finally `acknowledged` | |

Final cohort row on run 7: `settledDeliveryCount=2, nextGeneration=3, disposition=open, delivery=null` — with a terminal, never-delivered task. Children delegated *during* later wake turns (t12 on run 8, t14 on run 9, t16 on run 10…) each started fresh cohorts with reset counters, so their wakes worked — which is exactly why moderate parallelism masks the bug until one dispatch wave is large enough to stagger across ≥3 waves.

(The queued-delivery merging worked beautifully, for the record — t13/t15/t17 amending the queued wake into one bundled message is the right behavior. The problem is only the lifetime cap.)

### Suggested fixes (any of these)

1. **Make the cap a concurrency bound, not a lifetime bound.** The recursion the comment fears is "one delivery in flight + one reserved successor" — that's already bounded without a lifetime counter. Reset `settledDeliveryCount` (or simply drop it) whenever a sweep finds `pendingTaskIds.length > 0` after the delivery drains; the wake-per-terminal contract then holds and the parent still never sees more than one queued wake at a time.
2. **Sweep pendings on any parent-run settle.** Extend `handleTerminalRun` to arm a delivery for terminal app-owned tasks left `"pending"`/unarmed whenever the parent thread goes non-live. The existing generation + `alreadyDispatched` dedupe in `ProviderContinuationService.currentDelegatedCompletionDelivery` already guards against the duplicate-wake concern.
3. **At minimum, don't be silent.** If the cap stays, surface refused deliveries (system line in the thread: "N delegated results pending — read with task_status") and soften the tool description's "end the turn instead of polling," which is currently a trap.

Related smaller hole in the same family: for `mode="wait"` children (`settled_only`), `planDelegatedCompletionDelivery` returns with the task untouched (not even `"pending"`) when the parent has a live run — that branch precedes the pending-marking branches — and the post-timeout `wake-policy` upgrade knowingly skips re-planning when the parent settled in between ("a missed wake is cheaper than a duplicate one"). Same silent-starvation class, just harder to hit because the blocking wait usually owns delivery.

Happy to provide the raw projection rows or test this against a patched build — we run this stack daily.

@juliusmarminge one addition I'd really like here: **scheduled messages**.

I think this should be separate from normal queued messages. Queued messages mean “send after the current run finishes”; a scheduled message means “send this message at a specific date/time.”

The important architectural requirement is that the schedule must be persisted and executed by the **T3 server/environment that actually runs the agent**, not by whichever web/mobile/desktop client created it. If I schedule a message from my laptop or phone against an agent running on another machine, I should be able to close/disconnect that client and the message should still fire at the selected time.

In other words, the client should only create/edit/cancel the schedule. The host environment owns the durable record and dispatch timer.

A simple UX could be a “Send later” action from the composer that creates a one-shot scheduled message for the current thread. It should be visible/cancellable/editable before it fires.

I noticed this PR already adds server-persisted scheduled tasks, but those schedules appear recurring (`interval` / `fixed_time`). This feels like the same server-side scheduling infrastructure could support a one-shot `send_at`/timestamp schedule without conflating it with the existing queued-message semantics.

`apps/server/src/cli/app.ts:232-239` (Posted at PR level: an inline comment could not be anchored on this file in the current diff.) The `Effect.tryPromise` `catch` in `runAppCommand` collapses six semantically distinct failures into one error whose distinction survives only as an English sentence inside `cause: Schema.Defect()` — response timeout, oversized response, non-JSON response, schema-invalid response, request-id mismatch, and "connection closed" all become `DesktopAppUnreachableError`, whose message asserts the desktop app could not be reached and tells the user to start it. In the four response-shaped cases the app did answer, so that caller-visible message is wrong, and `cli/app.test.ts` asserts on the prose (`cause: { message: "The desktop app response is invalid." }`), which makes it behavior rather than diagnostics. The conventions ask that failures be distinguished by stable structural attributes with the message derived only from them, and that a translation boundary wrap only genuinely lower-level failures rather than flatten known ones. Consider having `sendDesktopAppActivationRequest` reject with tagged errors (or return a tagged result) so the CLI can keep `DesktopAppUnreachableError` for the connect-level `ENOENT`/`ECONNREFUSED` case its message describes, and add e.g. `DesktopAppResponseInvalidError { requestId, workspaceRoot, byteLength }` and `DesktopAppResponseTimeoutError { requestId, timeoutMs }` for the rest, each keeping the real socket error as `cause` where one exists. pull.body: ## Summary - wire orchestration V2 provider adapter registry/factory flow for Codex and Claude provider instances - add Claude replay/query primitives, native fork/rollback fixtures, subagent fixture coverage, and provider replay harness updates - update debugger model/provider picker and improve user-facing orchestration errors ## Validation - bun fmt - bun lint - bun typecheck - bun run test -- src/orchestration-v2/testkit/OrchestratorReplayFixtures.integration.test.ts -t claudeAgent - bun run test -- src/orchestration-v2/testkit/ClaudeReplayFixtures.integration.test.ts - bun run test -- src/orchestration-v2/testkit/ThreadFork.integration.test.ts -t Claude ## Notes - Draft PR for review of current branch state. Codex all-provider replay still needs schema alignment with latest app-server behavior before it can be treated as a full-suite signal. ## Closes Verified against the branch with code/commit evidence. ### High confidence Closes #4952 Closes #4873 Closes #4775 Closes #4795 Closes #4710 Closes #4668 Closes #4619 Closes #4584 Closes #4561 Closes #4713 Closes #4198 Closes #4452 Closes #3797 Closes #4232 Closes #3666 Closes #3580 Closes #2785 Closes #2789 Closes #3138 Closes #1404 Closes #231 Closes #216 ### Medium confidence (under review) Closes #4568 Closes #4766 Closes #4495 Closes #4456 Closes #4399 Closes #3744 Closes #2921 Closes #3624 Closes #3149 Closes #2336 Closes #538 Closes #2173 Closes #2065 > [!NOTE] > ### Introduce orchestration V2 runtime, services, provider adapters, and MCP toolkits > - Adds a complete orchestration V2 server runtime: projection store, event store, effect outbox, command receipts, checkpoint capture/rollback, thread management, run execution, provider session management, context handoff, runtime policy, and legacy V1 thread importer, composed through [runtimeLayer.ts](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/pull/2829/files#diff-30c4fe2818a050e1c3b89d70f25bba98ae53c42a26c7ab2fe70598ea812dd052) > - Adds V2 provider adapters for Codex, Claude, Cursor, Grok, OpenCode, and ACP Registry with a shared adapter contract, driver registry, and selection-transition policy > - Adds MCP toolkit services and HTTP registration for orchestrator delegation, thread operations, worktree handoff, project lifecycle, attachments, environment preferences, and preview controls > - Adds scheduled-task persistence, scheduling logic, server service, client runtime atoms, and a settings UI surface > - Migrates client-runtime and web/mobile UI from legacy session/turn fields to V2 projection-based runtime/run state, including thread details panel, queue controls, relationship graph, history loading, and item inspector > - Registers database migrations 050–061 for V2 foundation tables, subagents, provider-session bindings, launch workflows, application event sourcing, effect cancellation, scheduled tasks, legacy import state, and recovery/shell indexes > - Risk: replaces the legacy `EnvironmentApi` orchestration interface with `orchestrationV2`; removes `serverUpdateThreadContinuation` capability; `CursorSettings` no longer exposes `binaryPath` or `apiEndpoint`; `ProviderUsageLimitsIngestionLive` no longer subscribes to runtime events; thread routing resolves existing non-deleted threads directly to ready instead of loading > > > > Macroscope summarized 6102d00. > > --- > [!NOTE] > **Medium Risk** > Mobile thread persistence and list/archive/stop behavior change with V2 runtime semantics; removing the thread-transfer report workflow reduces PR visibility into transfer budget regressions. > > **Overview** > This slice of the orchestration V2 rollout **retires the thread-transfer PR comment pipeline** (trusted publisher script, tests, and `workflow_run` workflow) while CI can still emit transfer artifacts; it also **installs `build-essential` in CI** so ACP process-tree fixtures compile instead of soft-skipping. > > **Mobile** moves onto shared V2 client-runtime pieces: SQLite cache uses `ORCHESTRATION_CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION` and stored V2 shell/thread snapshots, runtime wiring swaps in bounded thread snapshot loading and history control, and thread detail/review/archive flows read **projections** (`runtime`, `RuntimeRequestId`, checkpoint summaries from `runId`) instead of V1 session/turn shapes. UX additions include **activity inspector**, **queue control**, **relationships banner**, progressive **history controls**, server **visit** watermarking, stricter **archive** rules via `threadCanArchive`, and approval/user-input cards that honor **live vs dead** provider `responseCapability`. > > Smaller touches: shared **brand mark** module, new **uniwind adaptive color** tokens, desktop env test for user-data dir names, README link to appearance docs, and marketing copy for Cursor harness. > > Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 9eeed8c17109be3752d2f8e1643583d1f579ea2d. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).
